sets.notes: Exact BSB quotes woven in with references, honest 'I think' framing on 5:11, and true-or-false explanations that state what the text says (e.g., 'It's the WHOLE law, not one command and done'). The weakest spots: the yoke is defined without a reference, 'Close to the feeling' for 'effort' is muddy, and humor is thin in places.

Accurate quotes with references on nearly every card, and the drawer line on 5:1 lands well. It falls into a 'You got it, baker / Not quite, friend' formula, slips into third person ('Papa Dorin always puts down his spatula'), and adds 'Paul is confident the Lord will deal with that person' on 5:10.

High energy and warm, with good kitchen pictures like leaven not 'staying politely in its corner.' It invents details ('his scars proved it,' 'He had to yell out'), breaks the food rule with 'one slice of the pie,' and cites only 'verse 1' instead of full references.

Mostly true to the text with clear corrections on each true-or-false card. It has almost no Papa Dorin voice or humor, opens many explanations with 'No,' tacks references on the end, and adds lines like 'confident in the Lord that the truth will stand.'

Punchy LOUD voice and some good lines ('Backward, friend. Backward.'). Most quotes carry no reference, it adds teaching the text doesn't give ('Leadership in the church… goes to those who serve,' 'nobody would be mad at me'), it uses salt, and it misspells 'à carte.'

It cites the verse in every explanation and reaches for drawer memories. It invents backstory and theology ('I know persecution,' 'I've seen fights in the drawer,' 'the royal law of love'), uses crude phrasing ('not the knife'), and mixes muddled images.

Short and generally accurate, with references on every card. It says 'wrong' and 'incorrect' about answers ('False is wrong here'), uses em dashes, adds commentary ('legalism,' 'false teachers'), and has no Papa Dorin voice.

Some quick kitchen images try for Papa Dorin's flavor. Nearly every explanation lacks a reference, uses em dashes, and runs under three sentences, with errors like calling 5:14 'the golden rule,' food-rule breaks (salt, sugar), and nonsense lines like 'hiding a cookie right out in the open.'
